subject: Acme procurement path & PO exception - next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acmecorp.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme procurement path & PO exception - next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from call:
- Acme procurement currently requires vendor setup before issuing POs; appears onboarding a new vendor can take 4–6 weeks.
- Purchasing team prefers POs / invoicing; corporate cards are not used for vendor spend.
- There may be a policy that blocks invoices to non-marketplace vendors unless an exception is approved.
- Finance asked about prepay options, minimum spend thresholds, and refund policy for pilots.

What we can do right now:
1) I attached a draft order form (redwood-orderform-draft.pdf) + SLA summary for your procurement team to review.
2) If Acme cannot issue a PO to a new vendor, we can support a short prepaid pilot (ACH) or pursue an internal procurement exception.
3) We can also investigate marketplace routes (AWS Marketplace) if that’s preferred by your vendor management team.

Can you confirm: (a) is an exception path required for new vendors, (b) whether prepay via ACH is acceptable for a pilot, and (c) what docs your procurement team needs (SOC2, vendor questionnaire, signed order form)?

Next steps: if you’re okay, I’ll fill out the procurement exception form and loop in Marissa (legal) to speed review.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-orderform-draft.pdf, redwood-SLA-summary.xlsx

From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acmecorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme procurement path & PO exception - next steps

Ben —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from procurement / finance: 
- Acme does not accept corporate card payments for vendor spend and we typically require a PO tied to an approved vendor ID.
- Adding a new vendor requires vendor onboarding (W-9, bank info, insurance) and legal review; timeline is ~4–6 weeks.
- We can consider an exception for small pilots but those require Procurement Director sign-off.
- Prepay (ACH) is allowed only with pre-approval; Finance will need a clear refund policy and service terms.

Can you send SOC 2 and standard vendor questionnaire answers? Also share the finalized order form and an estimate for a 1–3 month pilot (we're thinking ~$25k–$40k).

If you can fill the internal exception form (link below) and provide the security docs, Procurement will review it at the next Thursday committee meeting.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Chen
Procurement Manager | Acme Corp
sarah.chen@acmecorp.com

--- Forwarded link: https://intranet.acmecorp.com/procurement/exception-form

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acmecorp.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme procurement path & PO exception - next steps

Thanks Sarah — I've started the exception path. Attached: the initial exception request (acme-exception-request.pdf) and our security questionnaire answers (redwood-security-answers.pdf).

Proposal to unblock pilot:
- Option A (preferred): 6-week prepaid pilot for $25,000 via ACH; we'll issue a pro forma invoice and refund unused credits per the order form's terms.
- Option B: Expedite vendor onboarding and PO issuance (we'll provide W-9, bank details, insurance certs) — if Proc can start onboarding immediately, we can align contract date with PO issuance.

Marissa (cc) — can you review the exception request and the draft order form and confirm whether Legal can approve a pilot-level exception with our standard terms? If so, we'll sign via DocuSign (link below) and share invoice instructions for ACH.

DocuSign order form (draft): https://www.docusign.com/link/orderform/ACME-019
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-019

Ben

Attachments: acme-exception-request.pdf, redwood-security-answers.pdf

From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acmecorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme procurement path & PO exception - next steps

Ben / Marissa —

Reviewed the docs quickly with Finance. A few sticky points Procurement will want clarity on before approving an exception:
- Vendor onboarding still preferred; exceptions are rare and require Procurement Director + Legal sign-off.
- For prepaid pilots, Finance wants a statement of refund mechanics and evidence that Redwood will not retain customer data beyond agreed retention.
- We also need confirmation on indemnity and data residency (Acme requires EU data for EU customers).

If Legal can provide a trimmed exception with explicit refund terms and our requested security attestations, Procurement will present at Thursday's meeting. Can you get that to me by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks — Sarah

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acmecorp.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme procurement path & PO exception - urgent review needed

Marissa —

Escalating for quick review. Acme is asking for: explicit refund wording for a $25k prepaid pilot, confirmation on data residency for EU customers, and a short indemnity carveout acceptable to their Legal. Procurement will decide on Thursday; they asked for updated wording by EOD Wednesday.

Attached are the exception request and our security answers again. If Legal can draft a one-page addendum that (1) states refund mechanics for unused prepaid credits, (2) confirms we will honor EU data residency for scoped workloads, and (3) limits indemnity exposure for pilot usage, that should be sufficient for Procurement. If you approve, I can push DocuSign for signatures and provide ACH invoice instructions.

Let me know if you need me to set up a quick call with Sarah.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: acme-exception-request.pdf, redwood-security-answers.pdf
